[[Image:Simple magic cube.svg|thumb|right|An example of a 3 × 3 × 3 simple magic cube.]]

A '''simple magic cube''' is the lowest of six basic [[magic cube classes|classes of magic cubes]]. These classes are based on extra features required.

The simple magic cube requires only the basic features a cube requires to be magic. Namely, all lines parallel to the faces, and all 4 [[space diagonal]]s sum correctly.<ref>{{cite book | title=The Zen of Magic Squares, Circles, and Stars: An Exhibition of Surprising Structures Across Dimensions | publisher=Princeton University Press | author=Pickover, Clifford A. | year=2002 | pages=400 | isbn=9780691070414}}</ref> i.e. all "1-agonals" and all "3-agonals" sum to

:<math>S = \frac{m(m^3+1)}{2}.</math>

No planar diagonals (2-agonals) are required to sum correctly, so there are probably no [[magic square]]s in the cube.
